executiveSummary: GM1641's 2025 identity, generalized boundary, centre, 24,502 residents, 16 neighbourhoods, eight BAG places and five logical road-border links are internally coherent, and the deterministic ten-preset, six-checkpoint, eight-service contract passes. Release is nevertheless correction-required. Maasgouw is structured by the Maas, Julianakanaal, Lateraalkanaal/Lange Vlieter, Maasplassen, islands and distinct defence reaches, not by one municipality-wide flood scalar. The canonical river preset holds 0.737566 m through T+72 and distributes impact in a population-led order that puts Maasbracht, Heel and Linne ahead of directly pathway-sensitive Stevensweert, Ohé en Laak, Osen, Eiland and Wessem. Official evidence differentiates the below-norm Thorn-Wessem reach, completed Heel works and later Maas2050 reaches; project state is neither failure nor all-clear. Four current Waterinfo observations are normal at their points, but local forecasts stop at T+24, so T+48/T+72 remain NoData. The static mobility graph omits a current Rijkswaterstaat closure of the Stuw Linne foot/cycle crossing, and repeated A2/A73 links are common corridors rather than additive capacity. Public sources identify Lange Vlieter/WML source dependencies, RWZI Panheel, water controls, the Claus energy node, providers, antennas, schools and cross-boundary acute care, but not live topology, reserve, acceptance, backup or restoration. Exact hazard, service and recovery claims must therefore be suppressed or labelled synthetic until a selected, time-valid scenario and auditable action/resource state exist; null, empty, stale and horizon-limited inputs remain Unknown/NoData, never zero, safe, open or available.

evidenceSources.publisher: Centraal Bureau voor de Statistiek / PDOK / Kadaster
evidenceSources.title: E01 — GM1641 official 2025 municipality, neighbourhood, place, safety-region and statistics inputs
evidenceSources.edition: CBS Wijken en buurten 2025; generated municipal/regional snapshots retrieved 31 August 2026; safety-region snapshot retrieved 2 September 2026
supports: Annual CC BY 4.0 CBS/PDOK inputs uniquely identify GM1641 as Maasgouw in Limburg and Veiligheidsregio Limburg-Noord, and report 24,502 residents, density 536/km², 29.4% aged 65 or older and 3,626 one-person households. The reference point [5.882021062714444,51.1733060834662] is inside the 2025 generalized boundary.

Sixteen neighbourhoods in eight districts sum to 24,505 residents, three above the municipal total (+0.012%); published households sum to 11,090 and rounded age-65-plus rows to 7,220. Deterministic allocation reconciles to 24,502 without rewriting observations.

Eight active BAG places are contained: Beegden, Heel, Linne, Maasbracht, Ohé en Laak, Stevensweert, Thorn and Wessem. Nineteen BRT labels use separate woonkern/deelkern/gehucht/buurtschap semantics and add smaller labels such as Brachterbeek, Osen, Panheel, Eiland and Laak. BAG/PDOK place data use Public Domain Mark 1.0.

District-heating and public-charging values are missing in all sixteen neighbourhoods; home value is missing once, cars per household twice, and several tenure/benefit fields once. Publisher null, suppression or non-applicability remains NoData, not zero. Annual residents omit tourists, marina/camping occupants, pupils, care users and through-traffic.

evidenceSources.title: E02 — Climate Adaptation Strategy for Maasgouw
evidenceSources.edition: Definitive draft dated 20 May 2021; current municipal climate-adaptation landing page inspected 3 September 2026; blanket reuse licence not stated
supports: The strategy identifies Maas and stream flooding, short intense rain, multi-day rain and groundwater as distinct mechanisms. Its combined potential-flood map is approximately a 1-in-10-year planning view and explicitly says depicted areas will not all flood simultaneously; it is not a live or single-event inundation footprint.

It locates drought/nature-fire attention west of the Maas around Beegderheide, Heelderpeel, Wessem, Thorn, Panheel and Pol, and places the strongest urban heat-island signal in Maasbracht with lesser signals in Wessem, Linne and Heel.

It identifies drinking-water/nature dependencies around Heel-Beegden and Lange Vlieter, plus warm-water quality risks including blue-green algae/botulism. These are planning mechanisms, not live quality, reservoir state, demand, capacity or incident observations.

Its sewer design discussion and strategy actions are policy context. They cannot calibrate every catchment, pipe, pump, groundwater condition or first-72-hour response. Preserve document date, planning evidence class, map caveat, coverage and absent blanket licence.

evidenceSources.title: E03 — Maasgouw defence reaches: Thorn-Wessem, Heel and Maas2050 programming
evidenceSources.edition: Current project pages inspected 3 September 2026; Maas2050 municipal factsheet dated 6 October 2022; page-level blanket reuse licence not stated
supports: Waterschap Limburg says the current Thorn-Wessem defence does not meet the applicable safety norm and is not high/strong enough for future protection; the definitive project decision is scheduled in 2026 Q3 and execution from 2027. Need and planning status are not evidence of an active failure.

The current Heel page at https://www.waterschaplimburg.nl/projecten/dijkversterking-heel/ describes that reinforcement as completed/high-water safe. That reach-specific project result is not a municipality-wide all-clear or proof of performance in an unspecified event.

The dated factsheet at https://www.waterschaplimburg.nl/publish/pages/7161/2022-10-06_wl_maas2050_factsheets_maasgouw.pdf lists Thorn-Wessem (7.9 km), Heel (3.0 km), Ohé en Laak-Stevensweert (13.9 km), Clauscentrale (1.4 km), Heel Sleydal (2.2 km) and Beegden (0.4 km) with different programme horizons/statuses. The older Heel label must defer to the current completion page.

Green dikes, the hard Maasboulevard defence and the Thornerbeek context require reach, alignment, legal norm, project/version date, current operational state and selected scenario. Programme geometry/status alone does not provide breach, overtopping, seepage, closure or inundation timing.

evidenceSources.title: E04 — Time-scoped Maas/canal observations and current Stuw Linne maintenance/access notice
evidenceSources.edition: Waterinfo observations retrieved 2 September 2026 18:03Z and forecasts retrieved 3 September 2026 04:29Z; Stuw Linne closure notice published 25 March 2026 and maintenance notice April 2026; Waterinfo CC0, RWS page-level blanket reuse licence not established
supports: Waterinfo provides four observations at 17:30Z on 2 September: Heel boven 2090 cm NAP, Heel beneden Maas 1416 cm NAP, Panheel sluis boven 2864 cm NAP and Stevensweert 2092 cm NAP, each publisher-classed normal. Point status is not inundation, defence performance or municipality-wide safety.

Heel boven, Heel beneden and Stevensweert have forecasts at T+1/+6/+12/+24 only, publisher-classed normal at those points; Panheel has no consumed forecast and no local record exists at T+48/T+72. Horizon gaps expire to NoData and cannot be held, interpolated into certainty or used as a 72-hour all-clear.

The RWS notice at https://www.rijkswaterstaat.nl/nieuws/archief/2026/03/hinder-voor-fietsers-door-onderhoud-stuw-linne-in-2026 closes the Stuw Linne foot/cycle bridge from 28 August through 4 September 2026 with a signed detour. It is active by date at the audit T0, but the notice gives no exact reopening timestamp or live confirmation.

The RWS maintenance page at https://www.rijkswaterstaat.nl/nieuws/archief/2026/04/vervolg-groot-onderhoud-stuw-linne-vanaf-4-mei-2026 describes work from May to early October on the third Stoney section using a cofferdam. Maintenance is current context, not proof that regulation has failed or that capacity is reduced, unless an operational source says so.

evidenceSources.title: E05 — Current regional high-water plan, 2021 learning evaluation and Maasgouw preparedness
evidenceSources.edition: RBP Hoogwater Limburg 2023–2026; 2021 VRLN learning evaluation; current municipal Denk Vooruit page inspected 3 September 2026; blanket reuse licence not stated
supports: The current regional plan covers Maasgouw, the Maas and streams/tributaries and sets coordinated roles and prepared tasks. It is a planning document through 2026, not evidence that a warning, evacuation, reception site, route, asset or resource is active or complete.

The 2021 evaluation at https://www.vrln.nl/sites/vrln/files/2022-10/Leerevaluatie_Hoogwater_Maas_en_Roer_VR__Limburg_Noord_2021_rapportage.pdf records mandatory evacuation from 15 July, an 800 m emergency big-bag/sandbag wall at Maasboulevard Wessem, flooding/evacuation at Comfortparc Wessem and controlled return/cleanup. It is a historical case, not a current forecast or reusable automatic action.

That evaluation records that a requested Defence high-clearance vehicle for returning Osen residents could not be supplied because the resource was scarce. Assignment or request is not delivery; resource state and completion evidence matter during the first 72 hours.

The municipality's current https://www.gemeentemaasgouw.nl/denk-vooruit guidance frames household preparation for 72 hours, including 3 litres drinking water per person per day, medical needs and official alerts, and says the municipality can arrange temporary reception. Guidance and institutional capability are not measured household stock, reserved capacity or activation.

evidenceSources.title: E06 — Heel-Beegden/Lange Vlieter drinking-water source process and intake-stop context
evidenceSources.edition: Current operator process and Beegderheide pages inspected 3 September 2026; WML 2023 intake-stop retrospective; blanket reuse licence not stated
supports: WML monitors Maas water at Eijsden, can stop intake on contamination, routes suitable water through the Lateraalkanaal to Lange Vlieter and retains it for more than a year before production. This establishes source-process dependency, not live quality, storage, plant output or reserve.

WML reports that 2023 had 34 intake stops lasting at least one day, totalling 115 days, while stored water and groundwater could be used. Historical frequency and designed fallback do not prove availability, capacity or endurance for the audited 72-hour scenario.

The current Beegderheide page at https://www.wml.nl/over-wml/nieuws/brongebiedbeegderheide-routes says approximately 1.4 billion litres of groundwater are extracted annually to supply Maasgouw and Leudal and are combined with treated Maas water. Annual production context is not an incident-time service percentage or customer topology.

No reviewed public operator source supplies current customer connectivity, pressure/quality, failure state, emergency power, priority users, repair resources or restoration estimate. Those fields remain Unknown unless WML authorizes a time-scoped aggregate.

evidenceSources.title: E07 — Claus energy node and Linne hydroelectric context
evidenceSources.edition: Current operator/location and municipal Clausgebied pages inspected 3 September 2026; Claus C reactivation statement dated 1 October 2020; blanket reuse licence not stated
supports: RWE identifies Claus C as a gas-fired power station reactivated in 2020 with 1,304 MW stated capacity, and says it also operates the Linne hydroelectric plant. Nameplate capacity and operator identity do not establish current output, availability, fuel, grid path or local islanding.

The municipality's https://www.gemeentemaasgouw.nl/toekomst-clausgebied page calls the Claus area a nationally significant energy node with RWE generation and TenneT/Enexis substations. It is strategic/planning context, not live electrical topology or a cyber target state.

A large generating asset inside the municipality must not be interpreted as assured local customer supply. Conversely, a named energy node does not prove outage, cyber compromise, criticality ranking or sensitive connectivity.

Only authorized, time-scoped operator aggregates may drive power/gas/cyber restoration. Public nameplate and planning evidence may remain visible as non-causal context with source, date, scope and absent blanket licence.

evidenceSources.publisher: Het Waterschapshuis / Stichting Mijn Aansluiting / Netbeheer Nederland / RDI / DUO / RIVM
evidenceSources.title: E08 — Public water-control, provider, grid-planning, communications, education and acute-care context
evidenceSources.edition: Deployed public snapshots retrieved 31 August–3 September 2026; HWH CC BY-SA 4.0, Mijn Aansluiting Public Domain, DUO CC BY version unspecified, RIVM v1.1 CC0; exact NBNL/RDI licences not established in consumed metadata
supports: The HWH clip contains 37 realized assets: nine sewer pumps, fifteen surface-water pumps, RWZI Panheel and twelve weirs. Thirty-five capacity fields are null; the other two lack a displayed comparable unit/connectivity. Points do not establish topology, current control, reserve, power/telecom dependency or backup.

A point-territory lookup identifies Enexis electricity/gas, WML drinking water and Ziggo telecom, with September 2025 provider update dates; drainage is empty. One BUGG/Enexis NBNL planning sample includes demand/injection queues and projects, but it is planning context, not current load, spare capacity, outage or municipal topology.

RDI returns 61 antenna records and DUO 15 school records. Locations do not prove coverage/backhaul/power, emergency communications, shelter designation, occupancy, staff or supplies; licence/cadence remains explicit or unknown rather than inferred.

RIVM v1.1 finds no acute hospital inside GM1641. Laurentius Ziekenhuis Roermond is approximately 8.39 km from the municipal centre by straight line and reports 24/7 acute functions; distance and annual capacity are not route time, acceptance, staffing, backup or surge state. No local PM2.5 point exists.

identity.summary: GM1641, Maasgouw, Limburg and Veiligheidsregio Limburg-Noord agree across official/generated 2025 records.
notes: Feature id, bundle code/name, province, safety region and 2025 boundary/statistics editions agree.
The generated centre lies within the generalized municipal boundary.
No identity, region or headline-population contradiction was found.

geography.summary: Administrative geometry is coherent but cannot represent Maasplassen water/land edges, canals, islands, defence reaches, catchments or fire/heat mechanisms.
notes: Municipal and neighbourhood centroids are not hydraulic cells, defence alignments, breach/overflow pathways, stream/sewer catchments, heat surfaces, fuel polygons or utility territories.
Stevensweert, Ohé en Laak, Osen, Eiland, Wessem, Thorn, Heel and Maasbracht require source-specific full-resolution land/water, defence and access geometry.
Place and neighbourhood labels are navigation context, not hazard zones, evacuation areas or event-time population surfaces.

demography.summary: Municipal and neighbourhood totals reconcile within official rounding, with a high older share and transient-population caveats.
notes: CBS reports 24,502 residents; sixteen neighbourhood rows total 24,505 (+3, +0.012%), consistent with rounded cells.
Households total 11,090 and rounded age-65-plus residents 7,220; the headline age-65-plus share is 29.4% and one-person households number 3,626.
Annual residence does not measure tourists, marina/camping occupants, pupils, work populations, road/waterway users, home-care needs or assisted-evacuation requirements at event time.

regionalDetail.summary: Most 36 neighbourhood statistics exist, but missing variables and public infrastructure registers remain scoped context.
notes: District heat and charging are NoData in 16/16 rows; home value, cars per household and several tenure/benefit fields also contain gaps.

Water assets, provider territory, grid planning, generation, antennas, schools and hospital registrations retain publisher, version, retrieval, licence/unknown-licence, coverage and evidence class and remain non-causal.
Counts, nameplate values, queue totals or realized status never imply connected topology, compatible units, current operation, spare capacity, backup or restoration.

settlements.summary: Eight BAG places are contained and BRT correctly adds smaller settlement labels with different semantics.
notes: Beegden, Heel, Linne, Maasbracht, Ohé en Laak, Stevensweert, Thorn and Wessem are the eight active BAG places contained by the generalized boundary.
Nineteen BRT labels comprise ten woonkernen, five deelkernen, three gehuchten and one buurtschap and must not be conflated with BAG places or separate population controls.
Neither dataset establishes flood/fire footprint, evacuation zone, service area, seasonal occupancy or incident population.

transport.summary: Static NWB/GTFS context omits the current Stuw Linne walking/cycling closure and cannot establish 72-hour route throughput.
notes: The graph has five logical links to Echt-Susteren, Roerdalen and Leudal via A2, A73 and N273; repeated A2 and A73 ids represent the same physical corridors in series/across borders, not independent 260-unit capacities.
The active-by-date Stuw Linne foot/cycle bridge closure and signed detour are absent from the graph and zero bounded NDW records cannot supersede the authority notice or mean open.

There is no ProRail station inside and 33 GTFS stop areas are schedule/geometry only. No reviewed input supplies current service, vehicle/role throughput, bridge/lock state, waterway access or emergency/freight route capacity.

emergencyContext.summary: Current plans and guidance plus 2021 lessons identify roles and actions, but no auditable active resource ledger supports T0–T+72 consequence/recovery.
notes: The regional plan is valid planning context; 2021 evacuations, the Wessem emergency wall and Osen resource shortfall are historical lessons, not automatic current actions.

No public input supplies current defence/control decisions, evacuation/reception state, route clearance, acute-care acceptance, utility crews, emergency water/sanitation/power, stock/fuel or confirmed completion.
Household 72-hour preparation is guidance, not measured supplies or a restoration guarantee.

scenarioMatrix.summary: All ten canonical presets execute at T+0/6/12/24/48/72 across all eight services for GM1641.
notes: Initial focused audit:model passed the complete deterministic contract: one test file and two tests in 31.69 seconds.
A separate focused diagnostic enumerated all preset/checkpoint outputs, service values and neighbourhood rankings and passed one test in 14.58 seconds.
Scenario execution coverage is verified; this does not establish local physical or operational calibration.

numericalInvariants.summary: Bounds, reconciliation, determinism, service arithmetic and cumulative burden invariants hold.
notes: Availability values remain in [0,1], UI/sim-core preset factories agree, repeated runs are exact, demand/delivery reconcile and event-attributable person-hours are monotonic.
At T+24 severity spans 0 for earthquake to 0.944972 for compound; bounded arithmetic and six-decimal output are not evidence of observed precision.
Synthetic outputs must stay explicitly distinguished from timestamped observations, forecasts and official scenarios.

spatialPlausibility.summary: Water, heat and wildfire outputs lack local mechanism geometry and distinct hazards reuse a population-led neighbourhood order.
notes: River T+24 reports 0.737566 m, severity 0.232976 and 5,764 affected without a selected Maas hydrograph/datum, canal/defence reach/state, connected inundation, arrival or recession; T+72 retains the depth and increases affected to 6,316.
Pluvial T+24 reports 0.373584 m and 3,643 affected without a rainfall hyetograph, AHN depressions, soil/groundwater, sewer/catchment/control geometry or receiving-water state.

Every affected preset is led by the same population order: Maasbracht, Heel, Linne, Thorn, Wessem/Beegden, Stevensweert, Brachterbeek, Ohé and Eiland-Brandt. That does not follow Maas/island exposure, the strongest heat signal at Maasbracht, or the named western fire/drought areas.
Wildfire T+24 reports zero direct fire and affected persons but nonzero smoke and service burden. This is the preset's placement, not a conclusion of zero local fire risk.

serviceDependencies.summary: Eight service balances calculate, but water, energy, telecom, mobility, care and supply topology/state are unavailable.
notes: River T+24 availability is power 0.721398, water 0.678131, drainage 0.584496, gas 0.811575, telecom 0.660944, mobility 0.879227, facilities 0.732658 and supply 0.452273; no operator validates these exact values.

Compound T+24 availability is power 0.394000, water 0.379264, drainage 0.308221, gas 0.555534, telecom 0.222764, mobility 0.804785, facilities 0.503260 and supply 0.637440; these are aggregate synthetic percentages.

Lange Vlieter/WML context, 37 water-control assets, provider points, one NBNL planning sample, Claus/Linne generation, antennas, stops and hospital registration do not supply live connectivity, flow/load/quality, backup, switching, staffing, stock or restoration.
NWB edges and asset presence may inform context only; they must not become utility, communications, drinking-water, drainage, care or supply topology.

causalTrace.summary: Synthetic ledgers close, but missing hydraulic, fire, access, lifeline and authority-action dimensions do not gate displayed consequences.
notes: Hazard contributions, service-stage deltas and weighted service-loss contributions reconcile, and public observations/planning/context layers remain non-causal.
No selected source event supplies Maas/canal boundary, rainfall, defence/control state, footprint, fire ignition/perimeter, cyber target, operator outage, hospital acceptance or confirmed action.

Waterinfo is timestamped and quality-scoped but stops at T+24; the Stuw Linne notice is a current scoped access restriction. They require governed adapters and cannot silently calibrate unrelated hazards/services.
Unsupported exact depth, affected, availability and burden values must be marked synthetic screening/Unknown locally and expose missing dimensions on maps, briefs and exports.

recovery72h.summary: Persistent and recovering impacts through T+72 are deterministic but unsupported by hydraulics, operators, routes, care state or confirmed actions.
notes: River holds severity 0.232976 and depth 0.737566 from T+24 to T+72 while affected increases 5,764 to 6,316 and burden reaches 437,715.91; every service except facilities is exactly unchanged and facilities falls 0.732658 to 0.618536 without hydraulic or operational cause.

Compound severity falls 0.944972 to 0.498885 from T+24 to T+72 while depth stays 0.459127, affected rises 13,369 to 14,415, pressure rises 0.527280 to 0.557576 and burden reaches 941,151.13; service changes lack action/repair evidence.

Pluvial, storm and winter direct effects clear to zero by T+72 while burdens persist; coastal has zero direct affected at T+24 but degraded services. These patterns are not validated by recession, dewatering, inspection, repair or resupply evidence.
Only confirmed validity-aligned warning, defence/control, access, care, utility, logistics and welfare actions may alter recovery. Seventy-two hours is preparedness scope, not a restoration promise.

findings.summary: Generated identity, settlements, regional membership and 2025 demographic controls are coherent.
findings.evidence: GM1641, Maasgouw, Limburg, Limburg-Noord, the contained centre, eight BAG places and annual population agree; sixteen neighbourhoods total only three more residents than the municipal control and reconcile exactly.
findings.action: Retain source edition/retrieval time, full-resolution geometry access, published-versus-allocated values, null semantics and evidence class on refresh.

findings.summary: Null variables, empty local feeds and missing forecast horizons remain Unknown/NoData.
findings.evidence: District heat/charging are null in all sixteen rows, 35/37 HWH capacities are null, provider drainage is empty, NDW has no bounded record, Waterinfo has no local T+48/T+72 forecast, KNMI local weather and RIVM PM2.5 are absent, and no hospital is inside.
findings.action: Preserve publisher, version, retrieval/issue/valid time, licence or unknown licence, spatial/temporal coverage, evidence class, NoData mask and reason. Never coerce absence to zero, normal, dry, safe, open or available.

findings.summary: The river preset assigns unsupported depth and population-led impact without Maas/canal boundary, defence-reach or connected-footprint state.
findings.evidence: River holds 0.737566 m from T+24 through T+72 and reports 5,764 then 6,316 affected, but names no hydrograph/datum, Thorn-Wessem/Heel/Ohé-Stevensweert/Claus reach state, breach/overtopping/seepage, connected cell, arrival or recession.
findings.action: Suppress decision-facing river depth, affected counts, percentages and hotspots until an authority-governed scenario binds hydrograph/station/datum, defence reach/state, direct versus indirect pathways, footprint, timing, uncertainty and NoData. Retain general flood preparedness.

findings.summary: Official defence evidence is reach- and edition-specific, but the model exposes no defence state.
findings.evidence: The current authority calls Thorn-Wessem below norm, Heel completed and high-water safe at its reach, and dated Maas2050 material assigns other reaches later programme horizons. None establishes failure or municipality-wide protection for an unspecified event.
findings.action: Retain authority line geometry, reach id, norm, assessment/project edition, work status and validity as planning/static context. Require a selected official scenario plus current breach/overtopping/closure/inspection state before causal use; never translate planned reinforcement to failed or completed reach to all-safe.

findings.summary: Four point observations and forecasts through T+24 cannot validate or extend the simulated T+72 flood state.
findings.evidence: Waterinfo classifies Heel boven, Heel beneden, Panheel sluis boven and Stevensweert observations as normal; only three points have forecasts, ending at T+24. No local T+48/T+72 forecast or municipality inundation/defence state exists.
findings.action: Separate observations, forecasts, official scenarios and synthetic outputs. Show station/parameter/unit/datum, quality, issue/valid/retrieval time and horizon; expire absent horizons to NoData and never equate point-level normal with safe.

findings.summary: Pluvial, heat and fire outputs omit source-specific local mechanisms and reuse a shared population ranking.
findings.evidence: Pluvial T+24 reports 0.373584 m and 3,643 affected without rain, terrain, soil/groundwater, sewer/catchment/control or receiving-water state. All affected presets lead with the same population centres, despite official heat concentration at Maasbracht and western fire/drought areas around Beegderheide/Heelderpeel/Wessem/Thorn/Panheel/Pol.
findings.action: Replace shared demographic hotspot logic with governed mechanism-specific geometry. For pluvial use rainfall, AHN/BGT/BRO/land cover, catchments/sewer inclusion, controls and boundary levels; for heat/fire use canopy/paving/vulnerability and fuel/moisture/ignition/wind/smoke/access. Otherwise render local distribution Unknown.

findings.summary: The current Stuw Linne pedestrian/cycle closure is missing from the static mobility graph.
findings.evidence: Rijkswaterstaat closes the Stuw Linne foot/cycle bridge 28 August–4 September 2026 with a signed detour, active by date at audit T0. NWB/GTFS do not carry it and the bounded NDW query returns zero records; empty coverage is not open.
findings.action: Retain static NWB geometry but overlay the authority restriction with mode, segment, start, end/unknown exact time, issue/retrieval/freshness, reason and detour. Do not extend it to road/emergency modes, infer reopening without confirmation, or count repeated A2/A73 logical edges as independent capacity.

findings.summary: Lange Vlieter, groundwater and fallback context cannot support exact drinking-water availability or recovery.
findings.evidence: WML documents Maas intake monitoring/stops, Lange Vlieter retention and Beegderheide groundwater, while HWH identifies water assets including RWZI Panheel. No public source gives current storage, quality, customer topology, pressure, emergency power, reserve, priority users or repair state, yet river T+24 water availability is 0.678131.
findings.action: Show source/process and asset points only as non-causal context. Drive service state only from authorized time-scoped WML/water-board aggregates with quality, coverage, validity and uncertainty; otherwise label water/drainage availability synthetic/Unknown and do not infer resilience from storage or fallback descriptions.

findings.summary: Claus/Linne generation and provider/grid-planning records do not establish local power, gas or cyber state.
findings.evidence: RWE states Claus C is a 1,304 MW gas plant and operates Linne hydro; the municipality identifies a national energy node, and public records show Enexis territory/planning. These do not prove current output, grid path, local islanding, outage, cyber compromise, spare capacity or restoration, yet exact power/gas/telecom percentages are emitted.
findings.action: Retain named assets/nameplate/planning as non-causal context with date and scope. Accept only authorized operator aggregates/manual overrides for current state and recovery; never infer assured local supply or sensitive topology from asset presence.

findings.summary: Older residents, transient occupants and cross-boundary acute care are absent from operational service/supply claims.
findings.evidence: Age 65+ is 29.4%; no acute hospital is inside, and Laurentius Roermond is approximately 8.39 km straight-line from the centre. Annual resident and hospital records do not supply event-time tourists, assisted evacuation, route access, acceptance, staffing, oxygen/medicine, backup, fuel or resupply state.
findings.action: Model care/logistics across municipal boundaries using authorized aggregate acceptance/diversion, route/mode state, critical utilities/backup, staff/supply and issue/valid time. Keep identities and annual demographics separate; missing operational fields stay Unknown.

findings.summary: No auditable current first-72-hour action/resource ledger governs consequence or recovery claims.
findings.evidence: The regional plan and public guidance describe conditional warnings, barriers, evacuation, reception and emergency supplies; the 2021 case shows an 800 m Wessem barrier, evacuation/return and an unmet Osen vehicle request. The simulation consumes no current decision, assignment, resource, state, completion or expiry.
findings.action: Add Unknown-first records for warnings, defence/water controls, bridge/road/transit/waterway restrictions, evacuation/reception/return, care diversion, emergency water/sanitation/power, welfare checks, food/fuel/medicine, utility crews and mutual aid. Only confirmed valid actions may alter recovery.

findings.summary: Storm, winter, coastal, earthquake and cyber outputs remain bounded but locally uncalibrated exercises.
findings.evidence: There is no local KNMI observation in the consumed snapshot and the Limburg warning is level zero only within its publication horizon. One historic ML 0.7701 event near Heel on 6 January 2026 is not a T0 event or calibration; no direct coastal pathway or named cyber event/target is selected, while zero-direct presets still create service burden.
findings.action: Retain these presets only as clearly synthetic exercises, separate direct local from indirect regional effects, and bind a versioned observation/forecast/official scenario/target before operational use. No record, zero direct output and a shorter-horizon no-warning publication never imply broad safety.

corrections.summary: Gate GM1641 river and pluvial consequences behind selected hydraulic, defence, catchment, groundwater and rainfall mechanisms with strict Waterinfo horizon semantics.
corrections.validation: Without a governed source event, exact river/pluvial depth, affected counts, percentages and hotspots render Unknown/unsupported; fixtures preserve station/hydrograph/datum, reach/state, boundary/catchment/control, footprint, timing, release/licence, uncertainty and NoData, and T+24 forecasts never fill T+48/T+72.

corrections.summary: Replace shared population-led hotspots with source-specific Maasgouw flood, heat and fire/smoke geometry.
corrections.validation: River fixtures follow selected island/defence/connected-inundation cells; heat reflects canopy/paving and vulnerability; fire requires explicit ignition/fuels/moisture/wind. No footprint or ignition renders distribution Unknown/not simulated, never population-ranked or zero-safe.

corrections.summary: Overlay typed, time-valid Stuw Linne access restrictions and physical-corridor semantics on static transport data.

The Stuw Linne walking/cycling restriction is authority-backed and active by date, but no exact reopening time/live confirmation is supplied; it must not be generalized to other modes or retained beyond its scoped validity without a new check.

Static NWB, GTFS, provider, generation and care records omit event-time route/waterway/transit passability, emergency/freight throughput, hospital acceptance, shelters, assisted evacuation, seasonal occupants and household stocks.
Affected population is a people-equivalent scenario index and deprived person-hours is weighted local service deprivation, not casualties, evacuations, patients or customer interruptions.
Water, weather, defence, fire, access, care and utility state can change after audit completion; stale, empty, partial or out-of-coverage data must degrade to Unknown.
